transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The president of Iran says his country is still ready to follow through with a proposed
seven-day plan it presented to the U.S.
It's aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reports President Trev projected the proposal on Saturday.
In an interview with CBS's Face the Nation that aired on Sunday, Masoud Pezashqyan said
that after the seven-day milestone, and once mutual blockades are lifted, Iran was willing
to sit down for broader talks to formally end military conflict and address its nuclear
program.
In the interview, Pezashqyan said that Iran does not seek to develop nuclear weapons and
defended its civilian nuclear program.
Pezashqyan also addressed the lack of public appearances by the new Supreme Leader following
U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed his father.
The Iranian president said he had met the new leader twice and that he was healthy.
President Trump said on Saturday that he rejected Iran's seven-day proposal, but that he was
still open to negotiating.
Hadil Al-Shelchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
U.K. officials say they foiled a suspected terror plot near an airbase in western England.
The U.S. uses the base to launch attacks on Iran.
Police responded to a phone call in the middle of the night and intercepted several vehicles
close to the base.
Five men have been arrested.
Maggie Blythe is acting chief constable for the Gloucestershire Constabulary.
Again, I can't go into details, but I can give reassurance that we believe the matter
to be contained.
And as a set of agencies working together across Gloucestershire, we're gathering and
responding to local intelligence all the time.
President Trump claimed the suspects were under investigation and were looking to do
damage.
U.K. authorities have not confirmed this.
China and the U.S. have released a list of imports they will reduce tariffs on that are
worth $30 billion in each direction.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports from Beijing.
This follows last week's U.S. visit between President Trump and Chinese President Xi.
President Trump has been imposing rounds of tariffs on Chinese exports in his first and
now second term.
China retaliated in kind, often targeting Trump's voting base, American farmers.
Now they get some reprieve.
China's Commerce Ministry says it will lower tariffs on U.S. agricultural products like
beef, chicken, almonds, and also on American medical equipment and coal.
In exchange, the White House says it will reduce tariffs on Chinese baby products, toys,
and decorations, which, if implemented in time, American consumers could see some holiday
savings.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Over the weekend, President Trump said he is relaxing new fuel economy standards for
cars that will take effect today.
Following the rules could mean that cars won't go as far on a single gallon of gas.
This comes as AAA reports.
It costs $4.48 on average now for a gallon of regular gas.
You're listening to NPR.
Forecasters say a powerful nor'easter is weakening on the East Coast.
One person died over the weekend after they were hit by a falling tree.
The National Weather Service says there will be heavy rain up through New England today
before the storm tapers off.
The nor'easter brought strong winds, waves, and rain to the island of Nantucket this weekend.
On Saturday, residents discovered ship remains that may trace back to 1884, and Piers Isabella
Gomez Sarmiento reports.
The editor-in-chief of the Nantucket Current was covering the storm when he received a
tip about wooden fragments from what appeared to be a ship washed up on a beach.
Jason Graziadei went out to see the remains.
He told NPR they were in the same spot as ship parts found in 2022.
At the time, researchers spent months investigating the found wooden parts, which resembled a
ship's hull.
They concluded that the remains likely belonged to the Warren Sawyer.
It was a Boston-bound cargo ship that crashed in 1884.
Although it's not certain yet whether the new remains were once part of the Warren Sawyer,
Graziadei wrote to NPR that it's fascinating to encounter a piece of Nantucket's maritime
history.
This is Isabella Gomez Sarmiento, NPR News.
Separately, Hurricane NOLO is pulling away from the Hawaiian Islands.
It never made landfall, but NOLO may soon reach Category 5 status, the top of the hurricane
scale.
NOLO's outer bands of wind and rain struck the big island of Hawaii.
Separately on Mexico's Pacific Coast, powerful Hurricane Polo is expected to make landfall
in Baja, California.
That could happen late tonight.
This is NPR.
